newsitem.title: USA: Jury rules in favor of Michael Jackson.
newsitem.headline: Jury rules in favor of Michael Jackson.

text.p: A jury ruled on Tuesday in favour of Michael Jackson in a suit by five former employees alleging wrongful dismissal after they testified in a child molestation case against the reculsive pop star.
The jury also ordered two of the plaintiffs to pay Jackson $60,000 in damages.

Three former bodyguards, a maid and an administrative assistant also had charged in their civil suit that Jackson used recording devices at his Neverland ranch outside Santa Barbara in an attempt to find out what they knew about the abuse allegations.

In 1993 a 13-year-old boy sued Jackson, charging the singer molested him. The lawsuit was settled out of court for a reported $15 million and Jackson, who denied any wrongdoing, was never charged with a crime.
The jury of 10 women and two men said there was no evidence to support the charges against Jackson or the six aides mentioned in the lawsuit.
Jackson's attorney Steve Cochran said the star was happy with the verdict. "We're happy to be finally and fully vindicated," he said.

The jury also found in Jackson's favour on a counter complaint which charged two of the former employees had taken items from the ranch. Adrian McManus, a maid, was ordered to pay $35,000 in damages and Ralph Chacon, a member of the security staff, was ordered to pay $25,000.

One of the jurors said the she had a hard time believing the former employees after the jury learned the plaintiffs had sold their story to tabloids. "They lost their credibility when they went to the tabloids," said Lorie Durnin.
Michael Ring, who represented the plantiffs, said they were upset with the verdict after a six-month trial.
"They feel the evidence was there," Ring said.
